intro: Pick up any Qur'an, in any country, and it has the same shape. It has 114 chapters, called surahs. It has about 6,200 verses, called ayahs. It is split into 30 parts so it can be read in a month. In this unit you will learn that map. You will find out why the long surahs come first, what the labels Meccan and Medinan mean, and where three famous passages sit.

But the Qur'an is not only a book on a shelf. Muslims believe it was spoken before it was written. So this unit also follows the sound. You will meet the rules for reciting it, the people who know it all by heart, and the nights of Ramadan when it is heard from start to finish. You will see how the words became beautiful writing on walls and pages.

By the end, you will be able to find any verse from its two numbers, explain what a juz' and a hafiz are, and describe why Muslims keep the Arabic even when they read a translation. You will describe all of this the way a careful student does: "Muslims believe," "the Qur'an says," and "historians note."
bigQuestion: How is the Qur'an put together, and how do Muslims keep it alive in voice, memory and art?

timeline.t: Muslims believe the first words of the Qur'an, from surah 96, come to Muhammad in Mecca
Muhammad moves from Mecca to Medina; the Muslim calendar begins from this year
Muhammad dies; his followers know the Qur'an by heart and in written pieces
As Muslim tradition tells it, the leader Uthman has a standard written copy made
The oldest surviving Qur'an pages, like the Birmingham folios, are written on animal skin
The Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem is finished, with Qur'an verses on its walls
Dots and vowel marks are in common use; Ibn Muqla sets rules for beautiful letters
George Sale publishes the first full English translation made from the Arabic
Scholars in Cairo print a carefully checked edition that most Qur'ans follow today
Marmaduke Pickthall, an English Muslim, publishes The Meaning of the Glorious Koran
Millions of memorizers, Ramadan recitations and apps keep the Qur'an alive as sound

words.d: a chapter of the Qur'an; there are 114
a verse of the Qur'an; the word also means "a sign"
one of the 30 roughly equal parts of the Qur'an, often read one per night in Ramadan
labels telling which city Muslims believe a surah was revealed in
"The Opening," the seven-verse first surah recited in every daily prayer
Qur'an 2:255, a verse about God's power that many Muslims memorize
"In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," the line at the head of 113 surahs
to say aloud from memory, with care and rhythm
the rules for saying each sound of the Qur'an correctly
a person who has memorized the whole Qur'an; a woman or girl is a hafiza
a written or printed copy of the Qur'an
the art of beautiful handwriting, the main art of the Qur'an

test.q: How many surahs are in the Qur'an?
test.why: The Qur'an has 114 surahs, or chapters.

choices: Page 112, line 4
Surah 112, ayah 4
Juz' 112, part 4
The 112th word of surah 4
test.why: The first number is the surah, the second is the ayah.

test.q: Why is the Qur'an divided into 30 juz'?
choices: Because there are 30 prophets
Because each juz' is one surah
So the whole book can be read in one month
Because Arabic has 30 letters
test.why: One juz' each night finishes the Qur'an in the 29 or 30 days of Ramadan.

test.q: Which is true about the order of the surahs?
choices: It follows the time they were revealed
It goes shortest to longest
It is alphabetical
After surah 1, it runs roughly longest to shortest
test.why: The book's order is roughly by length, not the order Muslims believe the verses came.

test.q: What does the label "Medinan" on a surah mean?
choices: Muslims believe it was revealed in Medina
It is about the city of Medina
It is the longest kind of surah
It was written by scribes in Medina
test.why: The label names the city where Muslims believe the surah was revealed.

test.q: Which surah do Muslims recite in every unit of daily prayer?
choices: Surah 9
Al-Fatiha, surah 1
Surah 96
Surah 27
test.why: Al-Fatiha, The Opening, is part of every unit of prayer.

test.q: Which surah has no Bismillah at its head?
choices: Surah 1
Surah 2
Surah 9
Surah 112
test.why: Surah 9 is the only surah without the Bismillah at its start.

test.q: What does the name Qur'an mean?
choices: The book of law
The opening
The straight path
The recitation
test.why: The name comes from an Arabic word for reciting or reading aloud.

choices: The rules for reciting the Qur'an correctly
A style of writing
A written copy of the Qur'an
The ninth month of the year
test.why: Tajwid is the set of rules for each sound, stretch and pause when reciting.

choices: A person who leads a mosque
A person who has memorized the whole Qur'an
A person who translates the Qur'an
A person who prints the Qur'an
test.why: A hafiz knows the whole Qur'an by heart; the word means keeper.

test.q: What does surah 97 say about the Night of Power?
choices: It is the first night of Ramadan
It is the night of the hijra
It is better than a thousand months
It is the night the Kaaba was built
test.why: Surah 97 calls the Night of Power better than a thousand months.

test.q: Which sentence uses the word mushaf correctly?
choices: She recited a mushaf from memory.
Ramadan is the mushaf of fasting.
He followed the mushaf rules for pausing.
The mushaf sits wrapped in cloth on the top shelf.
test.why: A mushaf is a physical copy of the Qur'an, so it can sit on a shelf.

test.q: Why were dots and vowel marks added to the Qur'an's pages over time?
choices: So readers who did not know the words by heart could read them correctly
To make the book shorter
Because gold ink was cheap
To change the meaning
test.why: The marks helped readers, especially non-Arabic speakers, say the words the same way.

test.q: Why do mosque walls carry Qur'an verses and patterns instead of pictures of God?
choices: Paint was not available
Most Muslims believe pictures of God and the prophets should not be made
The Qur'an forbids all art
Only kings could be painted
test.why: Most Muslims do not make images of God or the prophets, so words and geometric patterns are the art.

test.q: Why did Pickthall call his 1930 translation "The Meaning of the Glorious Koran"?
choices: Because he translated only the meaning of surah 1
Because the publisher liked the name
Because he held that only the Arabic is the Qur'an
Because it was the first English translation
test.why: Pickthall, like most Muslims, saw a translation as the meaning, not the Qur'an itself.

write.prompt: Why do Muslims say the Qur'an is meant to be heard, not only read? Use two or three passages from this unit, such as 96:1-5 (Read!), 73:4 (recite slowly) and 97:1-3 (the Night of Power). Tell what each passage says and how Muslims act on it, such as tajwid, memorizing or Ramadan nights.
tips: Name each passage by surah and ayah, and the translation you used.
Say "Muslims believe" or "the Qur'an says" every time you give a belief.
Describe what Muslims do; do not say whether the belief is right or wrong.
Use the unit's words: surah, ayah, juz', tajwid, hafiz, mushaf.
End with one sentence that answers the question in your own words.
